title: Chickwheat Seitan Piccata
subtitle: with lemon, white wine and zucchini
menu_blurb: Crispy chickwheat seitan in a bright lemon, shallot, garlic and white wine pan sauce with zucchini, served over spaghetti with toasted almonds.
intro: This vegan piccata is super delicious. It gets its flavor from lemons, shallots, garlic, and parsley.
origin: “Piccata” is an Italian term meaning “pounded flat.” It usually refers to meat that has been pan-fried and served in a lemon, butter and caper sauce, and it is incredibly popular in the United States.

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: A knife, a pasta pot, and a large pan

prep_note: Make the [Chickwheat Shreds](recipe.html?r=chickwheat-shreds) ahead of time. They take about 2½ hours.

steps.title: Crisp the seitan
instructions: In a small bowl, mix the rice flour with the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, salt, and pepper, and toss the seitan in it.
Pan fry in olive oil with 4 of the minced garlic cloves until crispy, then move to a separate bowl.

steps.title: Cook the aromatics
instructions: Add the zucchini and sauté until half cooked.
Add the remaining 4 garlic cloves and cook for another minute.

steps.title: Make the pan sauce
instructions: Add the broth and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes.
Dissolve the arrowroot in a little water and stir it into the sauce.
Add the wine and let it simmer.
Stir in the lemon juice and ¼ cup of the parsley.

steps.title: Bring it together
instructions: Add the seitan and the lemon slices.
Let it sit until warmed through.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
instructions: While the sauce simmers, cook the spaghetti al dente ☺ and toast the almonds.

steps.title: Serve
instructions: Serve over the spaghetti, topped with toasted almonds and the rest of the parsley.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: The longer you marinate the seitan, the tastier it will be.

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Add mushrooms, swap the seitan for extra firm tofu, or swap the spaghetti for orzo or any pasta you like.

nutrition.notes: Over 90% water, which makes it great for hydration and weight management. Rich in vitamins C and B6 and antioxidants that support heart and vision health.
Rich in B vitamins, vitamin C, magnesium, and antioxidants that support heart health and reduce inflammation.
A good source of iron, and one of the most protein-dense plant foods available.

notebook.question: What is seitan?
answer: Seitan is a popular plant-based meat substitute made entirely from gluten, the main protein found in wheat. Often called “wheat meat,” it is prized by vegans and vegetarians for its dense, chewy, stringy texture.

notebook.question: Is seitan healthy?
answer: It can be an excellent, protein-rich addition to a plant-based diet.

benefits.label: High in protein
benefits.text: A 2-ounce serving packs about 17 g of protein.

benefits.label: Low in calories and fat
benefits.text: It contains almost no fat and very few carbohydrates.

benefits.label: Nutrient dense
benefits.text: It provides good amounts of iron, selenium, and calcium.

benefits.label: Soy-free
benefits.text: A great plant-based protein for anyone with a soy allergy. It does contain gluten.
